slides.say: p, q and r are consecutive even numbers, and zero is smaller than p, which is smaller than q, which is smaller than r. What is r squared minus p squared, over two q?

So p, q and r are positive even numbers in a row, in that order. The gaps are two, not one. We need the value of the fraction in the question. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, writing the numbers with one letter, and then plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Let's start with the middle number, q. p is the previous even number, so p is q minus two. r is the next even number, so r is q plus two. Now all three numbers are written with q.
The top of the fraction is r squared minus p squared. Use the difference-of-squares formula to write it as r minus p, times r plus p. We'll find those two parts separately.

First, r minus p. Replace r with q plus two, and subtract the whole expression q minus two. The q terms cancel. Two minus negative two is four, so r minus p is four. Now r plus p. That's q plus two, plus q minus two. The two and negative two cancel, leaving two q.
So the top is four times two q. The bottom is two q as well. Divide four times two q by two q. The matching two q cancels, leaving four. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: Now careful, choice number two comes from using a gap of one. These are even numbers in a row, so each gap is two. That's why we used q minus two and q plus two.
[pause] Now let's try plugging in numbers. We need positive even numbers in a row, so the smallest values we can choose are two, four and six. Use p is two, q is four, and r is six.

Calculate the whole top first. Six squared is thirty-six, and two squared is four. Thirty-six minus four is thirty-two. Now the bottom: two times q is two times four, which is eight. Thirty-two over eight is four. Choice number four is our answer. Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
